5.0.s.en: (1) The call to the people to hear the commandments

5.0.1.en: Keep: take care and be exact, because of the gravity of the words.

5.0.2.en: The second sermon begins with Moses' call to the people to give heed to hearing the Ten Commandments, which are God's statutes and His basic judgments for the people's conduct.

5.0.3.en: Then he asks them to take them in and understand their meanings deeply so that they may enjoy their power. The third thing Moses asked is that they do these commandments, so that they become life in them.

5.0.4.en: Turn everything you read in the Bible into practical application in your life, for approving and understanding the divine word is not enough, and may you take one verse each day, memorize it, repeat it and meditate on its meanings, so that this helps you apply it throughout the day.

5.1.0.en: Moses reminds them of the covenant which God made with their fathers at Mount Horeb, when He appeared to them in a great fire and mist on the mountain and gave them the commandments and the Law by the hand of Moses. When Moses came down from the mountain, he built an altar and twelve pillars as a confirmation of the participation of all the tribes in the covenant. He wrote the commandments and the Law in a book and sacrificed sacrifices and sprinkled the blood on the altar and on the people, confirming the covenant with blood, which is a type of the blood of Christ the Redeemer in the New Testament, by which we obtain salvation (Ex 24:6-8).

5.2.0.en: God made the covenant with the fathers who disobeyed Him by refusing to enter the Promised Land out of fear of those who lived in it, so He commanded that they be deprived of entering it, and they wandered in the wilderness until all the adult men died. Therefore the sons who are hearing Moses now might think that the covenant is not with them, so Moses affirms here that the covenant is with them and not with their fathers; this is God's intention, because God knows that the fathers will refuse to obey Him. He meant the sons who were children at that time or would be born afterwards, because they are the ones who will obey Him, so He will bring them into the land of Canaan. And with them, of course, were Caleb and Joshua.

5.3.0.en: To confirm the covenant, Moses declares that it was with God Himself and not by means of an angel or any mediator. What is meant by their seeing God face to face is seeing the fire on the mountain and hearing His voice, and this calls for holding fast to the covenant, the commandments and the Law, because they are from God directly.

5.4.0.en: Moses reminds them that he was a witness of God's presence and His speaking with the people, indeed he was a mediator between them and God, because they feared the sight of the mountain and the fire on it, so he drew near to the mountain and went up alone upon it and heard the commandments and the Law, and then told them to the people. After that Moses began to repeat the commandments to them, and therefore at the end of the verse it is written, "saying."

5.4.1.en: And just as Moses was a mediator between the people and God, so too Christ is the Mediator of the New Testament, who redeemed us by His blood and through whom we have access before the Father (Heb 8:6, Heb 12:24,.)

5.5.0.en: Before Me: that is, beside Me.

5.5.1.en: The first commandment is God's making Himself known to His people, and He makes the people know well that they did not come out of bondage in Egypt by their own strength, but that there was a lofty power able to bring them out, and this power is the power of Almighty God, and that He does not accept that His people worship other gods alongside their worship of Him, but He alone must be the God who is worshipped, without partner or equal.

5.6.0.en: In the second commandment the Lord forbids them to carve images for the purpose of worship resembling any of the forms found in heaven, like the planets, stars and moons, or found on the surface of the earth, like men and beasts, or found in the seas, like fish.

5.7.0.en: Bowing down is a bodily expression of submission and obedience from the one who bows to the one bowed to, and since God is the only Being to whom we owe this, He never allows bowing down to any other; even if there is no bowing down but standing in a spirit of reverence and submission, that is, worship, this too is not permitted to any but the one God. Hence the two expressions "thou shalt not bow down thyself to them" and "nor serve them" were necessary.

5.7.1.en: The Lord your God is a jealous God: in many places of the Bible the Lord likens His relationship with His people (His Church) to the relationship of a bridegroom with his bride or a husband with his wife.

5.7.2.en: Just as a bridegroom loves his bride and gives her every care and tenderness, he expects her to return love for love and tenderness with awe and submission. And a husband cannot bear that another person share in the love of his wife. So too the Lord is a jealous God who does not allow His beloved, that is, His people, to divide their love and worship, some of it for the true God and some for other gods, which would mean a loyalty to God that is not complete.

5.7.3.en: Here is a discussion of blessing and curse: the blessing which God bestows on those who love Him and keep His commandments, for love of God appears in holding fast to His commandments and doing them; and the curse that befalls those who do not love Him and hate Him in themselves, and its effects are reflected on their children after them. For the consequences of sin extend their effects to the following generations, as in the scattering of the Jewish people as a punishment for their rejection of Christ, whose effect extended to generations after the generation that rejected Christ.

5.8.0.en: A warning against the misuse of the name of God in any form, such as swearing by it falsely or in unseemly matters. A person must show complete reverence and utter respect for the name of the Lord, and mention it only with all awe and respect and only when there is real necessity. If a person transgresses this commandment, God punishes him.

5.8.1.en: This commandment keeps them away from using the names of the pagan gods, so that they swear only by the name of God, but with all esteem and respect. In Christianity, however, after spiritual maturity and steadfastness in the faith, swearing is not permitted, because the name of God is too high to be used in material dealings.

5.9.1.en: To sanctify it: to set it apart.

5.9.2.en: He commanded that the Sabbath day be set apart for the Lord, for it is a day for worship and rest from the usual daily works.

5.10.2.en: A person works six days of the week to provide for his material needs, but he needs to set apart a day of rest from work so that he may be free for worship. And God, who knows man's needs, commanded that man, beast and guest rest in all the cities of Israel, as well as the manservants and maidservants, reminding the people that they too were slaves in Egypt had the Lord not brought them out of their bondage by His great power, so they should care for the rest of their servants.

5.11.0.en: With this commandment begin the commandments concerning man's relationship with others, the most important of which is the relationship with his parents. God commands that every person care for his parents and meet their needs, so God prolongs his days on the earth in happiness with God, whether by the length of his life or by his delighting in his life with God. God promises many good things on earth to whoever cares for his parents, and then indescribable good things in the new land, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven. The sixth commandment:

5.12.0.en: Life is a gift from God; He gave it and He alone takes it, so man's life is sacred and must be respected and not violated in any form, otherwise God commands that the one who does this be punished by death, as He said from the days of Noah (Gen 9:6). The seventh commandment:

5.13.0.en: Adultery is a hideous sin, called in many places of the Bible "uncleanness," and because of it the Lord punished many peoples, beginning with the Flood and going on to the burning of Sodom and Gomorrah ... and the Lord Christ considered it a sufficient and sole reason for dissolving the holy bond of marriage.

5.14.0.en: Stealing is taking another's property, and it is most cruel in its effect on others since it deprives them of what they need, and the hideousness of this sin increases if the one stolen from is of the weak classes in society, like the widow and the poor.

5.15.0.en: If a person's testimony is required in court, he must neither add anything to the truth nor take anything from it, so that he wrongs no one, and show favor to no one, rich or poor (Deut 16:18-20). The tenth commandment:

5.16.0.en: Covetousness is an inner feeling of the heart and the first stage of the outward act that is to be condemned. Sin begins first in thought, and if we let this thought grow within us, it leads us in the end to the act. Hence the importance of the control of thought, which our Church calls for. This commandment fights sin at its roots, for if we refrain from coveting what belongs to others, we learn contentment and satisfaction.

5.17.0.en: And He added no more: that is, it needs no addition or increase, for it contains all the other legislation. At the end of his narration of the commandments, Moses the prophet affirms that they are the words of God which He gave him written on two tablets of stone when He appeared on the mountain, on which the glory of God appeared in mist, cloud and fire, and that these are the words of God and nothing is to be added to them.

5.17.1.en: May we be committed to carrying out God's commandments in our life, however great the pressures around us or the drifting of those around us into various sins, in order that we may enjoy God's care and blessings however much evil surrounds us.

5.18.s.en: (3) The people's fear of facing the Lord

5.18.0.en: The heads: the heads of the twelve tribes and their assistants.

5.18.1.en: The elders: the seventy elders chosen from the people to help Moses (Num 11:16). When the people saw the greatness of God in His appearing with fire and mist on the mountain and also heard His voice, they were greatly afraid, and showed this in their speech with the heads, marveling at the grace of God that allowed them to hear His voice and see Him, because they know that man cannot bear to see God.

5.19.0.en: In their great fear they declared to the heads their inability to see God again, lest His fire consume them and they die, because God's appearing is beyond man's capacity.

5.20.0.en: The people asked Moses to stand before God and speak with Him and then tell them what He wants, for fear of God's appearing to them again; but at the same time they were ready to obey Him in all that He commands, as Moses would tell them.

5.21.0.en: God praised the people's fear of Him and their readiness to obey Him, which they declared with their lips, and hoped that it would be in their hearts so that they would continue in this virtue and it would not be mere passing emotions.

5.22.0.en: God agreed to the people's returning to their tents because of their inability to continue seeing the glory of God, and it suffices that Moses stand before Him so that God may tell him the commandments and laws which he would teach the people, that they might live by them throughout their lives when they enter the land of Canaan.

5.23.0.en: Moses the prophet comments at the end, after he had recounted to them what happened at the receiving of the commandments and the Law, and asks the people to hold fast to God's word and carry it out, that they may live in peace and their days be prolonged in the Promised Land, filled with good things.

5.23.1.en: The fear of God is the beginning of the spiritual life, which ensures for you right conduct in His commandments and keeping away from sin. So always remember the greatness of God who stands before you, and you will live in purity and safety, and evil will not be able to enter you, and in the end you will secure the Kingdom of Heaven.

6.0.s.en: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

6.0.0.en: Before Moses mentions God's commandments and laws to the people, he warns them that the purpose of his words is that they do them after their entering the land of Canaan.

6.1.0.en: Carrying out God's word is the proof of their godliness, and he reminds them of the importance of doing these commandments not only in their generation but in all the coming generations, so that they may enjoy dwelling and settling in the Promised Land.

6.2.0.en: A land that floweth with milk and honey: an expression common among the peoples of that period for the fertility and goodness of the land, which the Promised Land enjoyed, especially in its northern part. He gives them the good news that if they carry out God's commandments exactly, they will obtain many good things and God will bless their number so that they increase and fill the Promised Land.

6.3.0.en: Before declaring the commandments, he reminds them that God is one, with no partner among the pagan gods, therefore his following words are of the utmost importance. This shows Judaism's call to the oneness of God among the peoples of the world who believe in a multiplicity of gods. Of course this does not conflict with faith in the Holy Trinity, that is, the essential attributes of God. There are indications of the Trinity in the Old Testament, and some see an indication of it in this verse, since the name of God is mentioned three times, as it says, the Lord, our God, the Lord. But the Trinity was declared clearly in the New Testament at the baptism of Christ in the Jordan River (Mt 3:16, 17).

6.3.1.en: Your faith in the oneness of God generates in you the fear of Him and respect for His commandments and striving to carry them out, and you also feel reassured in His hands because He loves you and there is no other god besides Him, so no one can harm you.

6.4.0.en: Since God is one and loved His people and cared for them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt and tending them in the wilderness, it is natural that His people love Him with a complete love, which he details as follows:

6.4.1.en: 1- With all thine heart: that is, the feelings.

6.4.2.en: 2- With all thy soul: which includes all of man's spiritual faculties, that is, the mind and the conscience.

6.4.3.en: 3- With all thy might: that is, all of man's bodily, that is outward, capacities.

6.4.4.en: In sum, the love of God with all of man's energy, inwardly and outwardly. Christ considered this verse the greatest commandment (Mt 22:35-39).

6.5.0.en: Moses demands of the people that God's commandments be their life and before their eyes at all times and that they repeat them always, but above all that they keep them in their hearts, so that they cover and contain all their feelings. And if they keep them in their hearts, that is, within them, they appear easily in their words and works.

6.6.0.en: Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children: since your heart is occupied with them, care to teach them to your children, so that they are established in your heart by your repeating them and your children live in them, and you encourage them and they encourage you to walk by them.

6.6.1.en: Thou shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house: that is, they are to be the first subject in your family life, so you repeat them in your chamber and in your house with your family, for repeating God's word establishes it in your heart, so that it is your first occupation in your inner and private life.

6.6.2.en: When thou walkest by the way: if you go to your work, do not neglect them but repeat them on the way as you go to your works and your engagements with others, so that they occupy your mind in every place you go to. And when thou liest down: they are to be on your tongue and in your mind even while you are on your bed, so that they are the last thing in your thought, and consequently your dreams and your subconscious mind are also occupied with them.

6.6.3.en: And when thou risest up: when you wake from sleep, you begin your day by repeating them, so you begin your daily life with them.

6.7.0.en: The Jews understood this commandment literally, so they wrote the commandment in small script and put it in a leather case and bound it on their hands. But what is meant is the spiritual meaning, that is, that the commandment cleave to everything to which your hands reach out, so that all your works are according to God's commandments.

6.7.1.en: And they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes: the band is a piece of cloth wound around the head to be like a turban, and the Jews also understood this commandment literally, so they wrote the commandments and put them in a leather case inside this band on the head, indeed they made their bands broad to contain the papers on which these commandments were written. Christ rebuked their concern for the letter of the commandment and their appearance and their neglect of its essence (Mt 23:5). What is meant is that the commandment be in man's thought always, because the head represents the mind.

6.8.0.en: The posts of thy house: that is, the main columns on which the house stands.

6.8.1.en: The Jews applied this commandment literally by writing it on the doors and the posts of the house, and what is meant by the gates is:

6.8.2.en: 1- Man's senses, that is, the entrances through which outward thoughts come in to him, so that God's word is the filter that sifts and purifies everything.

6.8.3.en: 2- The doors are what people enter by, so they signify our relationship with others, so that its foundation too is God's word.

6.9.s.en: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

6.9.0.en: God gives them the good news that they will possess in the land of Canaan cities, buildings, wells of water and lands planted with vines and olive trees which they did not labor to build, dig and plant, so that they may enjoy them and be filled with God's good things.

6.10.0.en: God warns them against being preoccupied with these good things when they find their material needs met and are settled, so that they forget Him, and He reminds them of His love, especially when they were in severe distress in Egypt and He brought them out by His power, so that they would not be influenced by the worship of idols or become attached to material things and leave Him.

6.10.1.en: Thank God for His gifts to you, but use them in measure, and do not indulge in your material lusts and rely on them so that your relationship with God weakens. Fasting and all that is connected with it of prayers and good works is necessary for your salvation.

6.11.0.en: God asked three things of them in their relationship with Him after their entering the land, which are:

6.11.1.en: Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God: so that you fear God and keep away from every sin or anything that angers Him.

6.11.2.en: And serve Him: offering the ritual worship of prayers and sacrifices and all that the Law prescribed, that their hearts may cling to His love and they may enjoy His blessings.

6.11.3.en: And shalt swear by His name: that the name of God be the decider in all their disputes and dealings, to protect them from swearing by pagan gods.

6.12.0.en: He stresses the need to beware of the worship of the idols which the peoples living around them in the new land worship, because all of them are vain and the works of demons.

6.13.0.en: He reminds them of His intense love for them as a bride of His own, for whom He cares and over whom He is jealous; so if they worship idols, the Lord will be angry with them and drive them out of the land of good things which He gave them, and this is what happened in the captivity.

6.14.0.en: Massah: a place near Rephidim where the people thirsted in the wilderness of Sinai.

6.14.1.en: He warns them, if they meet any tribulations, not to doubt the power of God who cares for them or His care for them, as they murmured against Him in the wilderness of Sinai when they thirsted in a place called Massah and said, "Is the Lord among us, or not?" (Ex 17:7).

6.15.0.en: Therefore he demands of them that they hold fast to His commandments and laws, so that they live in assurance, far from all murmuring and sin.

6.16.0.en: Instead of murmuring and sins, God calls them to do good and works of mercy with one another, so God will bless them and they will settle in the Promised Land from which God drove out its inhabitants because of their evil.

6.17.s.en: (3) Teaching children the fear of God

6.17.0.en: After their settling in the Promised Land, their children will notice their attachment to laws that differ from those of the other surrounding peoples, so they will ask their fathers the reason for their difference from the other peoples.

6.18.0.en: The fathers must explain to their sons God's care for them, by bringing them out of the land of Egypt with His strong hand by means of the ten plagues, then leading them in the wilderness of Sinai, and afterwards giving them possession of the Promised Land filled with good things, therefore they worship Him and hold fast to His commandments and Law, which distinguish them from the other peoples by God's care for them.

6.18.1.en: May you care to bring up your children spiritually and teach them the love and fear of God, and how to worship Him in the Church and thank Him at all times for His great works with them and His care for them, so that your faith and theirs in God is established in the midst of the wicked world.

6.19.0.en: Because of God's love and care, fathers teach their children to hold fast to His commandments and laws, so that it is well with them, and God counts that to them as righteousness, and they are established in the Promised Land.

6.19.1.en: From what has preceded appear God's grace with His people and His redemption of them from Egypt by the Passover lamb, but for the continued enjoyment of God's grace and His salvation, man's striving must appear in his holding fast to God's commandments. Therefore, in proportion to your sense of God's grace, hold fast to His commandments, and offer repentance every day for your sins and reject everything that leads to them.

6.19.2.en: The worship of God is the cause of His people's victory
